messages.subject: How to keep some variables not defined to split dataframe with ddply
messages.subject_clean: How to keep some variables not defined to split dataframe with ddply
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a data frame containing the following values (it is in long format) :

loghos = Identification number for a given patient
name = the name of the parameter corresponding to 'value'
value = the numerical value for the parameter considered on this row
sex = the patient's sex
date = the date the sample was collected for one patient

I want to get the minimal value for each parameter for each patient : this works fine with :

zmin = ddply(z4, .(loghos, name), summarise,
              value = min(value,na.rm=T),
               .progress="text" )

But i also would like to keep the date of the corresponding minimal value. I can't add date to the .variable field, because I don't want to split on date. When I try to code like that :

zminD2 = ddply(z4, .(loghos, name, statut), summarise,
              value = min(value,na.rm=T), date= date[which(value == min(value))],
               .progress="text" )

Here I get a date column in the result, but if I check, the date value is the minimal value of all date value for a patient, not the date corresponding to the minimal value.

Has someone any iea how I could code it ?

messages.body_plain:
As it happens so many times, I found the answer by posting the question :

Instead of using "summarize", I just wrote my own simple function :

zminD2 = ddply(z4, .(loghos, name,statut), function(m) {
i = which(m$value == min(m$value,na.rm = T))
return (m[i,])
})

So easy !

Thanks and sorry for those who spent time on this.

Sincerely

Julien

--

messages.subject: Using dlply to run mixed models
messages.subject_clean: Using dlply to run mixed models
messages.body_plain:
Dear manipulatr list,

I would like to use the dlply() command to run mixed effects models across subsets of my dataset.However, I get the following error message: "[...] invalid class “mer” object: Slot Zt must by dims['q']  by dims['n']*dims['s']"

Here is my command:

d <- sample(1:20, 50, replace=TRUE)                             # response variable
r <- gl(5,5,50,labels=c("A","B","C","D", "E"))                     # random effect
s <- gl(2,25,50,labels=c("g1","g2"))                                 # grouping variable (subsets)

dataset <- data.frame(d,r,s); dataset
attach(dataset)

library(plyr)
library(lme4)

# Mixed effect model using lmer (random effects only) does not work:
dlply(dataset, .(dataset$s), function(x) summary(lmer(x$d ~ 1 + (1|x$r))))

# However, linear models with lm() work just fine:
dlply(dataset, .(dataset$s), function(x) summary(lm(x$d ~ 1)))

I am using R 2.15.2 on Windows.

Thanks,
Viktoria

Hi:

This works for me:

dataset <- data.frame(d = sample(1:20, 50, replace=TRUE),
                      r = gl(5,5,50,labels=c("A","B","C","D", "E")),
                      s = gl(2,25,50,labels=c("g1","g2")) )

library(plyr)
library(lme4)

# Mixed effect model using lmer (random effects only) does not work:

tst <- dlply(dataset, "s", function(x) summary(lmer(d ~ 1 + (1|r), data = x)))

Notice two things:
(1) The data = x term inside of the lmer() call;
(2) The way dataset was defined.

messages.subject: accessing list item names in l*ply
messages.subject_clean: accessing list item names in l*ply
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Is it possible to access the name of each list item in the function to be applied ?
For instance, if L is a list containing dataframes named d1 to d5, and I want to write each one to a different file, named d1.txt to d5.txt

l_ply(L, write.table) should do the trick, but I cannot see how to have write.table get the name of the items.

As names(L[i]) gives the name of item i of the list L, I would have expected this to work :

l_ply(L, function(x) write.table (x, file=paste(names(x), ".txt", sep=""))

but it doesn't.
Any suggestion, please ?

Thanks,
Alain
